Subject: Re: Draft MAP and unit-econ worksheet

Hi Priya — thanks for sending the draft MAP. Diego and I reviewed the pricing worksheet and have two blocking questions before we can align internal stakeholders: 1) you have a single tokens-per-second (TPS) profile for the live inference workloads — can you send the per-endpoint tokens-per-request distribution you used for the model variant? 2) How does Redwood arrive at the tokens/$ number when caching is enabled? Our product team simulates heavy prefix reuse and we want to ensure the unit economics reflect prefix cache hit rates (0%, 30%, 60%).

We attached a short doc with our expected traffic slices and a one-pager of regulatory latency SLOs. If possible, can we get concrete cost scenarios (tokens/$) for the three cache-hit cases by EOD Wed 5/22? We need that for a pricing approval meeting Thurs morning.

— Samantha
Aurelius Labs | Senior Product Ops

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Samantha Nguyen <samantha@aureliuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-21T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and unit-econ worksheet

Priya / Samantha — answering the technical pieces so we have a single source of truth: 
1) Token accounting: Redwood reports billable tokens as the tokens emitted + the raw prompt bytes submitted to the model at the time of inference. For prefix/KV cache hits we have two levers customers choose in the MAP: 
   - Conservative billing: count full prompt tokens (no credit for cache) — used for procurement/forecasting safety.
   - Optimistic billing: charge only delta tokens (new tokens not present in KV cache) — used for pilot budgets and reserved capacity offers.
2) For the worksheet I ran a quick sim using Aurelius' traffic slices (attached) and our internal sample rates: median tokens/request = 420, p95 = 3,200. TPS profile is bursty (30s bursts every 6 minutes) — see stress-scenarios tab.
3) Cache hit modeling: I produced three columns (0%, 30%, 60%) and applied a simple linear reduction to prompt tokens for cacheable prefixes; model output tokens still count fully. Example: 30% cache => median billed tokens/request drops from 420 to ~314.
4) Batching: for hosted API we recommend small dynamic batching (inter-request latency 8–25ms) — improves throughput without materially changing per-request token billing, but reduces compute unit cost. For Dedicated, we can enable larger static batched windows for increased tokens/$ at the cost of added 10–30ms p95 latency.

I attached the sim output (token-econ-stress-scenarios.pdf) and updated XLSX (Aurelius_MAP_v1.3.xlsx) with the data. Priya — you can paste these numbers into the MAP. Samantha — let us know which billing posture you prefer (Conservative vs Optimistic) so Ben can draft the pricing anchor.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: token-econ-stress-scenarios.pdf (report)
Attachment: Aurelius_MAP_v1.3.xlsx (updated worksheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@aureliuslabs.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-21T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and unit-econ worksheet

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. Commercial notes / timeline: 
- If Aurelius wants Dedicated reserved capacity for production by July 15, we need a signed SOW and PO by June 17 (45-day provisioning & procurement window).
- Pricing anchor: using Karthik's optimistic delta-billing numbers (30% cache case) our list tokens/$ for hosted API is $0.037 per 1k tokens; Dedicated reserved contract starts at an effective $0.022 per 1k tokens for the modeled traffic (after commit). I can structure a two-stage discount (pilot -> commit) in the MAP.
- Legal: our standard SLA exception (90-day pilot, reduced uptime SLA) can be added to the MAP as a canary clause. If you need a security questionnaire response earlier, we can prioritize the SOC2 evidence pack.

Action items for Aurelius to close on timeline:
1) Confirm billing posture (Conservative vs Optimistic) — this materially shifts the unit economics.
2) Share procurement lead (name/email) to get PO timeline aligned.
3) Confirm pilot start window (we propose 6/03) and pilot success criteria (p95 latency <= 350ms, token burn within 10% of modeled 30% cache scenario).

I’ll draft a pricing appendix for the MAP and send it back by 5/22 EOD.

— Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: commercial-anchor-v1.pdf (pricing stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Samantha / Diego — attached is the consolidated MAP + MAP appendix with the cache-hit scenarios filled in and our recommended gating timeline. Highlights: 
- Tokens/$ scenarios:
   • 0% cache (hosted): median billed tokens/request = 420 -> tokens per $ = 23,810 (i.e., $0.042 per 1k tokens)
   • 30% cache (hosted, optimistic): median billed tokens/request = 294 -> tokens per $ = 34,029 (i.e., $0.029 per 1k tokens)
   • 60% cache (hosted, optimistic): median billed tokens/request = 168 -> tokens per $ = 59,523 (i.e., $0.017 per 1k tokens)
- Dedicated reserved effective rates (after a 12-month commit) are ~40–48% lower vs hosted list depending on batch sizing.
- Recommended MAP gating:
   1) 5/24 — Aurelius confirms billing posture and procurement lead (PRIYA action: compile contact details)
   2) 5/31 — Security questionnaire submitted (Redwood to attach SOC2 artifacts)
   3) 6/03 — Pilot kickoff (2-week smoke + 4-week functional)
   4) 6/28 — Pilot close decision (go/no-go for Dedicated)
   5) 7/15 — Production on Dedicated (if commit signed by 6/17)

Please see the attached MAP (Aurelius_MAP_v1.3.xlsx) and stress scenarios PDF. Ben will follow up with a pricing appendix; Karthik will support a brief tech call to walk your infra team through caching/batching tradeoffs. If you confirm the billing posture today we can lock the pilot slot for 6/03.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelius_MAP_v1.3.xlsx, token-econ-stress-scenarios.pdf, commercial-anchor-v1.pdf
